chapter: Inside the Basie rhythm section and band family
title: Walter Page
summary: Greene describes Page as a good timekeeper who gave breaks and held things together, and was well trained.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Well, one thing -- I mean, Walter Page was a very strong force in that.
Yes. Yes.
I mean -- what did he contribute that was sort of special?

Well, let's see. Walter was a good time keeper. Plus, he would, you know, along with the time, he would keep the -- keep, doing alot of breaks and solos in between, see. And, whatever amount of choruses he has, he'll be playing -- he'll play some times in between, and then he will keep the rhythm going. But, he would hold things together.
Because, Freddie, wasn't that before bass players really took choruses. See -- I mean they didn't take whole choruses in those days.
No, no.
He would get chunks, right?
Mm hmm. Mm hmm.
And, he would get chunks, and what-not, but --
Mm hmm. But, he didn't get too many solos, you know. I mean, whatever he did, he did while -- you know --
Yeah. Yeah.
-- other things were going on, see.
Yeah.
But, he kept everything straight. Going -- like straight ahead.
But, he was a well trained musician I've been told. That he had a better background --
Background, yes.
-- than alot of people.
Yes. Yes. He did.
And, that he also would step down -- well he used to play baritone sax at one time.
Oh. I didn't know that.
Yeah. Somebody told me that. That he would sometimes step down, pick up the baritone, and --
Oh, yeah?
--- play on it, you know -- show off his, I think Jo Jones told me that. That they'd be -- you know, that they'd be a little
Yeah. They had to be, because I don't remember him doing it.
Yeah. Yeah, yeah.
